subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted API vs current provider - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@finlytics.com>; Tom Nguyen <tom@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + p95/p99 targets (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can scope a short validation run: 

1) Current constraints you mentioned:
   - Concurrency target: ~50 concurrent active sessions for your web UI (peak).
   - Average sustained throughput: ~600 requests/minute during peak windows.
   - Current provider numbers (end-to-end, model request -> final token): p95 ~320ms, p99 ~780ms for non-streaming 1-shot generation of your summarization model.
   - Streaming: used for assistant-style chat sessions for some customers; you noted first-byte latency is important for UX.

2) Redwood hosted goals (what we typically target for similar workloads):
   - p95 end-to-end: <=200ms (non-streaming)
   - p99 end-to-end: <=450ms (non-streaming)
   - First-byte for streaming: <=150ms for cold requests, sub-50ms for cached prefixes
   - Support for sustained concurrency and autoscale to handle 50+ concurrent sessions with batching and KV cache.

3) Info we still need from you to finalize a short validation plan:
   - Exact payload sizes (avg prompt tokens and avg response tokens) — you estimated ~60 input tokens / ~40 output tokens.
   - Any IP restrictions for test traffic / whitelisted IPs for our test harness.
   - Which endpoints you want to exercise: hosted API (text generation + streaming) and the existing provider for side-by-side comparison.

4) Proposed next steps:
   - We’ll send a 2-week mutual action plan: 3 days of smoke tests, 3 days of full-load synthetic runs, then a production-like pilot for 7 days where we collect traces and token-level latency distributions.
   - Attachments: perf_matrix.xlsx (sample load spec) and redwood_mutual_action_plan.pdf (draft). Please review and flag changes.

Happy to run a short technical kickoff next week with our infra lead (Aditya) and your engineering lead to lock down the test harness. Are you available Tue/Wed next week for a 30-min sync?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cell: (415) 555-0123

Attachments: perf_matrix.xlsx (Excel, load/size targets), redwood_mutual_action_plan.pdf (PDF, draft MAP)

From: Priya Shah <priya@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + p95/p99 targets (hosted vs current provider)

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa — helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Payload sizes: confirmed ~55-70 input tokens (varies) and ~30-50 output tokens. We'll send a sample set of prompts by end of day Friday.
- Current provider numbers: the p99 you quoted is from their dashboard; our own traces show a tail closer to ~820ms during peak bursts (we can share a 24h trace).
- Streaming: yes, for our in-product assistant we stream partial tokens. The UX team calls out that time-to-first-byte (TTFB) needs to be <200ms for acceptable experience.

We're interested in the 2-week validation. Tue/Wed next week works; prefer Wed 10am PT. Can you include Aditya and a contact for your infra team?

We'll also need to run an internal procurement step for allowing Redwood test IPs — I'll loop in security if needed.

Priya
Head of Platform, Finlytics
priya@finlytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + p95/p99 targets (hosted vs current provider)

Perfect — thanks Priya. Wed 10am PT works for us; I’ll send a calendar invite.

A few notes ahead of the call so we can hit the ground running: 
- Team joining from Redwood: Aditya (infra lead) and Laura (solutions/eng). Aditya will propose the load harness & tracing hooks; Laura will run through expected observability artifacts we’ll share.
- Test plan highlights:
   * Smoke (3 days): validate correctness, auth, streaming handshake, and sample latency checks at low QPS.
   * Full-load synthetic (3 days): step traffic to 600 r/min with 50 concurrent simulated sessions, measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99, and collect traces.
   * Pilot (7 days): production-like traffic to validate caching effectiveness, failure modes, and steady-state tails.
- Data we will need from you in advance: sample prompts (you mentioned), sample traffic window (one day of traces if possible), and whitelisted IPs (if procurement requires it)

I attached an updated perf_matrix.xlsx with the load spec we discussed. Also included a short checklist in the MAP for procurement & security artifacts.

Next steps: calendar invite + link to a shared Drive with test harness and perf sheets.

Thanks — looking forward to Wed.
Marissa

Attachments: perf_matrix.xlsx (updated)

From: Tom Nguyen <tom@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finlytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + p95/p99 targets (hosted vs current provider)

Thanks Marissa — Wed 10am PT confirmed on our calendar. Quick note from engineering after reviewing the perf matrix: 

- We can send the sample prompts and a 24h trace by EOD today.
- We'd like the validation harness to capture per-request trace IDs so we can correlate with our client-side timing. Can your test harness preserve an incoming request ID header and echo it back in traces?
- One ask: when you run the synthetic full-load, please include a mix that exercises streaming (40% sessions) vs non-streaming (60%). That will reflect our real traffic.

If you can confirm request-id passthrough and the mix, we’ll proceed with procurement steps for whitelisting.

Best,
Tom
Sr. Eng Mgr, Finlytics

On Wed, 25 Feb 2026 at 11:10 AM PST, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Tom — yes, we can:
> 
> - Our harness supports an X-Redwood-Client-Request-Id header and will echo it back in spans and traces. We’ll include instruction in the runbook for correlating client timing with server traces.
> - We’ll configure the full-load mix as 40% streaming / 60% non-streaming and include token-level timing breakdowns plus first-byte statistics.
> 
> I’ve attached the final MAP and runbook link in the calendar invite. Looking forward to kickoff.
> 
> —Marissa
